To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quantum recurrence spectrum of classically chaotic system is highly resolved, that it is possible to extract information about complex orbits (ghosts) by analyzing the recurrence spectrum and that the quantum spectrum of classically integrable systems is not highly resolved, but rather is a superposition of the quantum recurrence spectrum and the quantum eigenvalue spectrum.

(a) the quantum recurrence spectra of classically nonintegrable systems are highly resolved and can be obtained by a harmonic inversion of quantum spectral data, (b) the harmonic inversion method uncovers complex orbits, (c) the quantum recurrence spectrum of the hydrogen atom is in agreement with semiclassical periodic orbit theory, (d) the quantum recurrence cross section of the hydrogen atom agrees with semiclassical closed orbit theory, (e) the quantum recurrence density of states of the hydrogen atom does not agree with semiclassical theory
the harmonic inversion method is a very useful technique for the analysis of highly resolved quantum recurrence spectra and that the results are sensitive to separate orbits and to complex orbits.
